title: Not a programmer, new dad, building a dark ARPG with AI help. Here's my story
author: Tobias-StaldieGames
selftext:
Hi everyone, I'm Tobi from Germany, the solo dev behind Ossaria.



I've played ARPGs since Diablo 2. A year ago I became a father and my gaming time shrank a lot. That's when I noticed how many ARPGs don't respect your time: crafting that can brick your item, systems where every upside comes with a punishment. So I started building my own, a dark ARPG where the best gear can be found by luck or crafted with certainty.

The catch: I'm not a programmer. Here's how I actually build it with AI.

I write the design myself in plain German: game design docs and a decision log where every rule I settle on gets written down. An AI coding agent (Claude) reads those docs and writes the C# code in Unity. I play every build, give feedback and decide what stays. Whenever I correct something, the fix also gets a small test rule, so the same mistake can't quietly come back later. That last part was the biggest lesson for me: without it, the AI kept breaking things it had already fixed.

What AI does not do: the art. All characters, monsters, environments and effects were made by professional artists, I bought their work. No AI-generated art in the game.

It's still early. The combat isn't good enough to show yet, so this video is just me explaining the why.

I'd love to hear from others here: how do you keep an AI agent from breaking older features in a growing codebase? And if you play ARPGs, what wastes your time the most?
